name: Urine albumin
rangeNote: Below about 20 mg/L is the usual screening limit in a first-morning urine sample; labs vary. A concentration depends on how much you drank, so the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) from the same sample is the preferred result. Hard exercise, fever, infection and menstruation can raise it, and a raised result is usually confirmed with repeat tests.
summary: Albumin is a blood protein. Healthy kidneys let very little of it into the urine; small amounts are sometimes called "microalbumin". This result is the amount per litre of urine, so it also depends on how dilute the sample is.

high.meaning: More albumin in the urine can be an early sign of kidney damage, but a single concentration can also be high because the urine is concentrated. The albumin-to-creatinine ratio and repeat tests show whether it is lasting. Discuss a raised result with your doctor.
commonCauses: Concentrated urine (drinking little before the sample)
Hard exercise in the day before the sample
Fever, infection (including a urinary infection) or acute illness

low.meaning: A low or undetectable result is normal: healthy kidneys keep almost all albumin in the blood. Very dilute urine can also make it look lower.
commonCauses: Dilute urine after drinking a lot
